lines: Phases 1 to 5 complete. Phase 6 in progress. The decision asked of Brandon in Status 236 at about 5:20 PM MT Friday stands unanswered: move on to the film and the masters, or one more round of looks first. The work goes on in either case and only the freeze waits.

Chain 41 is on main since 01:00 UTC (6:00 PM MT Friday): summer's see through swirl at the landing. Stated by the helper that ran it, every floor of the order is met: only summer's landing guard moved and equals its builder's, the four shakes measure 0.9694, 0.889, 0.9572 and 0.961 as in chain 40, summer at rest measures 0.8981 as in chain 39, the whole test run 1055 passed and 8 skipped. What I see beside the approved shake picture: tree, cottage glow and lamp posts read through the swirl; the streaks are whiter and coarser than the approved's fine warm swirl and the base is darker and browner than the approved's pale cream. Summer's landing stays below the bar. The live page is still round two (the twelfth publish); the first pictures for the thirteenth publish are being drawn on this head now.

Preview 07 is finished: rough draft 7 of the film with the prompt opening, 74.5 s, 960x540, 30 frames a second, with sound, drawn by four helpers on a tree whose sources equal chain 41's. In it: fall's darker air, the one smear for each flying petal and leaf, summer's see through swirl. Not in it: spring's glass mend and the patch for the stall at low quality. Measured: 2234 frames, every one of the twelve chunks on the same engine, no page message, no blue, dark or repeated frame in the scan. Two sheets looked at by me at preview size show no fault.

The final render on his own computer, first run on Windows. Measured by the builder of the one file on a hosted Windows Server 2025 machine with 2 cores and no graphics card, not on his computer: the four install lines run as written in PowerShell in a folder with a space in its name; setup passes with the same engine hash as on Linux; the doctor read the processor, memory, card, Chrome and free disk by itself, drew one film frame at 3840x2160, saw that this machine draws in software and refused, as it must. Finding: Chrome on Windows draws through Direct3D 11, and its shader compiler warns on some of the film's shaders, which still compile and draw. One warning matters: the compiler may leave out the tests for a broken number that guard the glass, the frost and the frame's sum, so one bad sample could spoil a pixel or a block of a master on his card, and the same holds for every Windows visitor of the live page. Whether any frame really differs there is unknown. Decision 249: it is mended now on its own branch (tests the Direct3D compiler cannot leave out, with the eight guard pictures held equal on Linux and the Windows doctor as the proof), and the doctor will print what his card's compiler answers, so the short test on his machine says by itself whether the guards work. No final render is started in the cloud.

Spring's glass after a shake: its builder states the mend stands on its machine (heads and trails at the landing as at rest, the other seven guards equal); it merged the new main and measures again; its whole report comes about 7:05 PM MT, later than its aim.

Remaining in phase 6 and what he receives. The thirteenth publish at the same address: chains 40 and 41 live (fall's darker air, the petals' smear, summer's swirl), after the first pictures and the security review. Chain 42: spring's glass, the patch for the stall at low quality if it comes whole, summer's fireflies and the seeds' dots, the petals' weave, the frost line; then a fourteenth publish. The render instructions: one file in the repo and one line to give Claude Code; its builder's own guess for the last report is about 2:00 AM MT Saturday. On his word the freeze: the repo goes private and the references are redrawn. Then the film steps of the build order (card loop, judged stills, record round, preview films, proof of the local render, cue sheet, README, last publish, gauntlet) and the full 4K 60 render on his gaming PC on his word: With Prompt and Without Prompt at 3840x2160, the Portfolio Looping Video and the Portfolio Screenshot. Last, a fresh reviewer's score against the showcase standard.

Open, below the bar: summer's landing streaks and base as said above; summer's pond at rest, flat pale plates where the approved has dark water (item 279); fall's storm paler than approved; spring's glass bare after a shake on the live page (mend being measured); spring's fence and trails; the fireflies' flat bars at 4K (item 276); the seeds' lumps of dots at the stills' close camera (item 277); the weave in the petals' smears at film frames 1388 and 1389 (item 278); the frost line at film frame 668 (item 275); the stall at low quality on a software renderer; winter's four small items; fall's near fence and the pumpkin's stepped face (item 272); the petals' fringe at film frame 680; the poster tool that stops on one failed request (item 273).
Sound credits 7,420 of 10,000 (measured from the ledger at 01:07 UTC: 52 calls), no call since 05:47 UTC on Thursday (10:47 PM MT Wednesday). No film render; one new preview, Preview 07.
